summary.text: 明, “bright” or “clear,” has more than one ancient construction. The familiar 日 and 月 combine the sun and moon to suggest light or dawn. Another early form, 朙, places the moon beside a window; in that form the window contributes both an image and a sound cue.

formation.text: 明 combines meanings; the window variant 朙 also includes a phonetic contribution.

components.text: In 明, 日 is the sun. Its combination with 月 is already ancient, rather than necessarily a corruption of the window form.
The moon contributes light in both the sun-and-moon and moon-and-window constructions.
This window component belongs to the alternative form 朙. It suggests moonlight entering a room and also supplies sound.

sound.text: These modern readings differ in initial, vowel and tone. The window component’s sound role belongs to older Chinese, where the reconstructed forms share more material.
Both reconstructed forms contain mraŋ; 囧 additionally has initial k- and final ʔ. The shared material helps explain the historical sound cue without claiming identical pronunciation.

history.text: The variants should not be forced into one sequence. Sun and moon can evoke dawn or brightness; moon and window evoke moonlight indoors. Other spellings use an eye-like or field-like shape, some explained as copying changes.

uncertainties.text: The earliest eye-and-moon form is not securely identified as this character. Exactly how all the variant spellings relate remains uncertain.
